text:
Colorado outplayed Winnipeg for most of the night and still lost, and the final minute shows how. With the game tied 2-2 and the clock at 19:00 of the third, Kyle Connor wristed home a feed from Mark Scheifele for the winner. It was a 13% chance, one of only a handful the Jets generated, and it was enough.

The gap between play and result was wide. COL out-chanced WPG 2.84 to 2.02 in expected goals, led in shot attempts 68 to 50 and in shots on goal 34 to 19. The simulations say COL deserved to win 65% of the time. The first period was the clearest example: COL held a 1.03 to 0.31 edge in chances and had nothing on the scoreboard to show for it. Stuart Skinner did the rest, stopping 32 of 34 shots against an expected 2.84 goals, which put him 0.84 goals ahead of what an average goalie would have managed. Mackenzie Blackwood went the other way, allowing 3 goals on 19 shots when 2.02 would have been the norm. Nicolas Roy's 22% look in the second period was the best chance that stayed out.

The goals came in bursts. Jaden Schwartz opened the scoring at 2:51 of the second, Connor tied it 70 seconds later on a tip-in, and Cole Perfetti put WPG ahead with a deflection at 18:16. Fedor Svechkov tied it at 12:35 of the third with a tip-in, also set up by Schwartz, before Connor's second ended it. Neither team scored on the power play (COL 0 for 1, WPG 0 for 2).
